resolved.question: WP-1: Task 1 Postgres image — switch from pgautoupgrade/pgautoupgrade:18-alpine to postgres:16.4 or stay in pgautoupgrade family?
resolved.answer: Do NOT switch to postgres:16.4. The current image pgautoupgrade/pgautoupgrade:18-alpine is already effectively pinned (specific tag, not :latest). Switching to postgres:16.4 would be a PG18->PG16 downgrade requiring a data volume dump/restore — this triggers the §6 stop-and-ask. The PRD audit intent was to prevent tag drift, which is already satisfied. Task 1 should instead: (a) check if a minor-version tag like pgautoupgrade:18.4-alpine is available and more specific, and (b) document in a comment that the tag is intentional. No family switch. Rationale: brief §6 "stop if switch requires dump/restore"; data volume at PG18 cannot be read by PG16 without pg_dumpall/pg_restore.

resolved.question: PRD section 7.3 storage-cap eviction (per_peer_storage_cap=10000, oldest-unreviewed-row drop + ENTRY_KIND_FEDERATION_INBOUND_DROPPED_STORAGE_CAP_EVICTED) - does the eviction logic live inside wrap_governance_inbound success path, or inside each Phase-6 receive_remote_* handler?
options: option-a (advisor-resolved): at the Phase-6-handler insert path (where the advisory row is actually written), invoked uniformly so all 3 advisory tables (remote_sanction_notice / federation_attestation / remote_moderation_label) get the cap check; the wrapper post-inner success path is the uniform invocation point so the 3 receive_remote_* bodies are not each duplicated

resolved.answer: option-a. Storage-cap eviction happens at INSERT time per PRD section 7.3 verbatim (at insert time, check SELECT COUNT(*) FROM remote_sanction_notice WHERE source_instance = $1 AND admin_reviewed_at IS NULL. If >= cap, drop the oldest unreviewed row for that peer with a federation_inbox_dropped_log entry + governance_log federation_inbound_storage_cap_evicted). It is NOT one of the 5 pre-inner check helpers (those are reject-gates: trust/size/rate/actor-rate/replay, PRD section 9.2 steps 1-6 - none of which mutate the advisory tables). The cap check is coupled to the WRITE, so it belongs with the Phase-6 receive_remote_* insert path. To avoid duplicating it across all 3 receive_remote_* bodies, the plan factors it into a single helper (e.g. enforce_storage_cap(peer, table_kind, conn)) invoked from the wrapper post-inner SUCCESS path (after inner() returns Ok) so the behaviour is uniform across the 3 advisory types - OR, if the planner finds the post-inner point cannot know which table inner() wrote, invoked at the head of each receive_remote_* (the planner picks based on the actual Phase-6 handler shapes read at plan time and records the choice + rationale in section 10 + a kind:log). NOTE this is distinct from the eviction being a drop that returns an HTTP error - per PRD section 7.3 oldest-drop is NON-rejecting (the new inbound is still accepted; an OLDER row is evicted), so it does NOT return a 4xx and does NOT short-circuit inner(); that is why it is post-success, not a pre-inner reject-gate. The eviction writes (the evicted-row effect + federation_inbox_dropped_log + governance_log) are part of the multi-write transaction boundary (brief watchpoint #8, feedback_multi_write_handlers_need_transactions). Sources: PRD section 7.3 (verbatim insert-time mechanism + why oldest-drop, not reject), PRD section 9.2 (the 6 pre-inner steps that storage-cap is NOT among), plan v1-federation-inbound-a.plan.md section 10.7 + .claude/rules/governance-log-entry-kind-registry.md fed-in-a section (const shipped, -b emits).

The migration 2026-05-17 already seeded this key with value_int=100; raw INSERT would create a second row and the reader (get_inbound_config_int) returns an arbitrary one. UPDATE mutates the existing seed row in place." Once Tasks 1+2 land .order_by(valid_from.desc()), the claim "reader returns an arbitrary one" becomes false.
resolved.answer: Update in Task 3 (option update-comment-in-task-3). Brief amended to add Task 3 IMPLEMENT step (b): replace the existing workaround block with a one-line note explaining that UPDATE-in-place stays valid for historical continuity AND that INSERT-with-newer-valid_from is now also safe post-v1-federation-inbound-c (per DQ #324). Removing entirely (option remove-comment-entirely) loses the audit trail of WHY the existing test uses UPDATE; leaving as-is (option leave-comment-as-historical-context) misleads future test authors who read it and conclude they cannot use INSERT. The update-comment-in-task-3 path preserves both audit trail and accuracy.

resolved.question: v1-quality-r3c brief: what is the correct test shape for BREHON_DISABLE_FED_REPLAY_CLEANUP_JOB guard test? The brief says "call the scheduler tick" but the cleanup runs in an inline scheduler closure with no standalone function.
options: option-a: call delete_older_than() directly with window_days=1 and a seeded old row; set guard and assert row is NOT deleted (direct DB-function probe)
option-b: invoke the scheduler closure indirectly via a test harness; assert no DB mutations
resolved.context: Confirmed by reading scheduled_tasks.rs:396-461: the cleanup calls federation_inbox_nonce::delete_older_than(window_days_i64, conn) inline in a scheduler closure. delete_older_than is at crates/db_schema/src/source/governance/federation_inbox_nonce.rs:37. FederationInboxNonceInsertForm at line 30 has peer_instance: String + activity_id: String fields. delete_older_than deletes rows with seen_at < now()-window_days.
resolved.answer: option-a: The guard test must call delete_older_than() directly (not via the scheduler) because the scheduler closure is not callable from test context. Test shape: (1) seed a FederationInboxNonceInsertForm row with seen_at = now()-30days via diesel INSERT; (2) set EnvVarGuard BREHON_DISABLE_FED_REPLAY_CLEANUP_JOB=1; (3) call delete_older_than(1, &mut conn) directly — since the guard is checked OUTSIDE the function (in the closure body above the delete_older_than call), the test cannot test the guard via the function call alone; instead the test should mirror the guard check inline: if std::env::var(...)=="1" { skip assertion }; alternatively, the test tests the FUNCTION in isolation (seeded row is deleted when gate is not set; not deleted when gate is set AND we skip the call). RECOMMENDED: two tests — (a) gate=unset + call => row deleted; (b) gate=set + call => still call the function (guard is in the scheduler, not the function) but the test verifies the function deletes when called — then separately test the guard at integration level by asserting the scheduler path is not exercised. SIMPLEST viable test: one test that sets the guard and verifies no rows are deleted from federation_inbox_nonce (by directly querying the count) after a simulated scheduler tick interval. The plan §13 IMPLEMENT should describe this shape explicitly, citing federation_inbox_nonce.rs:30 for the insert form and :37 for delete_older_than.

resolved.question: RT-r5 rollup computation: should reputation_rollup_cron reuse recompute_snapshot(person_id, None) or use a dedicated weighted-average-of-per-community-snapshots helper?
resolved.context: Brief rt-r5-planning-1.md §5 flags this as the planner's key open question. Verified against code 2026-05-31: recompute_snapshot(conn, person_id, None, cache) at reputation_snapshot.rs:222 SUMS EVENTS via load_live_events (rs.rs:682), which filters reputation_event.community_id IS NULL — i.e. instance-scoped events only (founder seeds + instance-wide deltas). It does NOT aggregate per-community snapshots. PRD §5.5 specifies rollup.dimension = sum(per_community_snapshot.dimension * weight) / sum(weight) — a weighted AVERAGE of per-community SNAPSHOT rows, categorically different from an instance-scoped event-sum.
resolved.answer: dedicated-rollup-aggregation-helper. The rollup cron MUST NOT reuse recompute_snapshot(person_id, None) — that function event-sums instance-scoped reputation_event rows (community_id IS NULL), which is NOT the PRD §5.5 rollup (weighted average of per-community snapshot dimension values). The plan must introduce a dedicated aggregation path that: (1) loads all per-community snapshots for a person (reputation_snapshot WHERE person_id=$1 AND community_id IS NOT NULL); (2) for each of the 4 dimensions, computes sum(snapshot.dimension * weight) / sum(weight) with weight=1 per community (job.rollup_equal_weights=true default); (3) excludes banned-from communities from the denominator per OQ-V1-02 (active sanction with target_community_id set, scope Community) using the load_person_context sanction-detection pattern at reputation_snapshot.rs:736-768 as the canonical filter shape; (4) writes the result via upsert_snapshot (reputation_snapshot.rs:770) with community_id=None — reusing upsert_snapshot is correct (the WRITE path is shared); only the COMPUTE path must be rollup-specific. The capability-flip detection (detect_capability_changes + ENTRY_KIND_CAPABILITY_CHANGED with snapshot_community_id:null) and the ENTRY_KIND_ROLLUP_RECOMPUTED emit fire on the rollup row. Source: PRD §5.5 (weighted-average spec) cross-checked against reputation_snapshot.rs:222/682/736/770 (recompute_snapshot event-sum semantics). Planner: do NOT pass community_id=None to recompute_snapshot expecting a rollup; author a distinct helper (e.g. compute_rollup_snapshot or upsert_rollup_snapshot) that does the weighted average then delegates to upsert_snapshot for the write.

resolved.question: WP-1: How does the bridge authenticate to the new binary-side POST /governance/room-event callback endpoint? Option-a: shared secret (env var BRIDGE_CALLBACK_SECRET) checked server-side; option-b: bridge passes Lemmy admin JWT (requires the bridge to hold admin credentials in .env); option-c: the endpoint is unauthenticated but bound to localhost/internal network only.
options: option-a: shared BRIDGE_CALLBACK_SECRET checked in the handler (no Lemmy admin JWT needed)
option-b: bridge holds admin JWT in .env and sends Authorization header
resolved.context: admin_get_messaging_config (the brehon_read_url endpoint) already requires is_admin JWT. The bridge's soft_pause.rs polls that endpoint without any auth header (bare GET), which would fail is_admin — suggesting either the endpoint was not yet tested against a real server, or there is a separate unauthenticated endpoint. No unauthenticated bridge-callback route exists in crates/api/routes/src/lib.rs. The Phase 4 room-event callback needs an explicit auth decision before the planner can spec the handler.
resolved.answer: option-a (per user 2026-06-06): the bridge authenticates to POST /governance/room-event via a shared secret BRIDGE_CALLBACK_SECRET (env var, in .env) checked by a server-side middleware on the route, mirroring the bridge's existing hs_token/as_token bearer-token trust model (services/bridge/src/appservice.rs:52 hs_token_auth; provision.rs:23 bearer_auth(as_token)). The middleware checks Authorization: Bearer <BRIDGE_CALLBACK_SECRET>. Least-privilege (scoped to the one callback route, NOT the full is_admin surface); host-independent (survives the bridge/binary host-split the design doc anticipates at messaging.md:407); never expires (no JWT refresh path). This is service-to-service auth (bridge daemon <-> Lemmy binary), orthogonal to the end-user separate-login decision (ADR-016 line 282: users sign into Lemmy and Matrix separately; Brehon is NOT an IdP; B-actor portable-ID roll-up is M2-late, gated OQ-ADR016-03). The planner specs: (a) BRIDGE_CALLBACK_SECRET in BridgeConfig + .env; (b) a bearer-secret middleware on the new route (mirror hs_token_auth shape but in the actix/Lemmy binary's framework, not axum); (c) the same secret used on the bridge-read path to close the soft_pause.rs latent bug (see DQ a3d0e9941441-054).

resolved.question: WP-2: The bridge_room table provides restart-idempotency (no duplicate Room::Created per case_id) — which persistence store should it use? Option-a: rusqlite (embedded SQLite file, add rusqlite to services/bridge/Cargo.toml); option-b: sqlx with SQLite feature (adds sqlx dep); option-c: in-memory HashMap<case_id, BridgeRoom> (no SQLite dep, but lost on restart — restart-idempotency handled purely by replaying from last_seen_governance_log_row_id via binary API query on startup).
options: option-a: rusqlite embedded SQLite file (persistent, simple, no async overhead)
option-b: sqlx-sqlite (async, matches Lemmy toolchain style but adds heavy dep to bridge)
option-c: in-memory HashMap + replay from binary governance_log on startup (no new dep, restart-safe if replay is fast)
resolved.context: services/bridge/Cargo.toml has no SQLite dep (matrix-sdk, ruma-appservice-api, axum, tokio, reqwest, serde, serde_json, tracing, anyhow only). Phase 5 acceptance criterion requires no duplicate Room::Created on bridge restart. Option-c is viable if the binary exposes a GET /governance/room-events?case_id=X endpoint that returns already-written Room::* log entries so the bridge can skip re-provisioning on startup. This endpoint does not exist yet either, so option-c would add a second binary route. Option-a is the lightest path for the bridge crate itself.
resolved.answer: option-a (per user 2026-06-06): bridge_room uses rusqlite (embedded SQLite file). Add rusqlite to services/bridge/Cargo.toml. Durable across restarts (Phase-5 restart-idempotency is a stated acceptance criterion, not optional); bridge owns its own self-contained store (ADR-004 plane separation; PRD Decisions Log: 'bridge_room table in services/bridge/ (bridge-local store)... the bridge owns its own store'). Rejected option-c (in-memory + governance_log replay): forces a second new binary route (GET /governance/room-log), couples bridge startup to a network round-trip, and is lossy (the append-only hash chain records what was provisioned, not the bridge's full operational state: MXID<->room mappings, in-flight retries, OQ-009 per-room reveal state). Rejected option-b (sqlx-sqlite): async + compile-time query-check macro overkill for one tiny table; heavier compile. rusqlite is the standard right-sized embedded-store choice for a Rust daemon with local state, and gives a natural home for the last_seen_governance_log_row_id watermark + MXID mappings + reveal state in one place. Synchronous rusqlite calls run via tokio::task::spawn_blocking if they ever land on a hot path (bridge_room writes are off the provisioning hot path). Zero-Matrix-deps gate still holds: SQLite is workspace-excluded; cargo tree --workspace | grep -cE 'matrix-sdk|ruma' stays 0.

resolved.question: M1 latent bug: services/bridge/src/soft_pause.rs polls brehon_read_url (= admin_get_messaging_config) with a bare unauthenticated GET, but that endpoint requires is_admin (crates/api/api/src/governance/messaging_config.rs:165-183). Against a real running server it returns 401, so poll_once parses no messaging_enabled field and unwrap_or(false) makes the bridge read relay_enabled=false forever — silently never relaying. The M1 dm_round_trip soft_pause test is todo!() so this was never exercised against a live binary.
options: fix in m2-rooms-a Phase 4 alongside BRIDGE_CALLBACK_SECRET work
resolved.answer: Fold the fix into m2-rooms-a Phase 4 (the bridge<->binary auth task). Resolution: when adding BRIDGE_CALLBACK_SECRET (per DQ a3d0e9941441-052 option-a), add an unauthenticated-but-secret bridge-read endpoint (e.g. GET /governance/bridge/messaging-status accepting Authorization: Bearer <BRIDGE_CALLBACK_SECRET>, NOT is_admin) that returns {messaging_enabled: bool}, and repoint the bridge's BREHON_READ_URL / soft_pause.rs at it. The existing admin_get_messaging_config stays is_admin-gated for the human admin panel; the bridge gets its own service-principal read path on the same shared secret. This closes the silent-no-relay failure mode AND unifies the bridge's read+callback auth under one secret. Planner: add this as an explicit Phase 4 deliverable (one new binary route + one BridgeConfig repoint + un-todo! the soft_pause_enable_disable_cycle test in dm_round_trip.rs once the docker stack exists). The fix is NOT urgent on its own (M1 has no live messaging deployment yet — pilot server has no gov .wasm plugins and messaging_enabled is false), so a separate governance-v0 hotfix is unwarranted; m2-rooms-a Phase 4 is the right home because it builds the auth path anyway.
